title: Actual completion unit on a strict K-flat quotient cone
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $W$ under consideration assume $\ell$ invertible on $W$, use its small pro-etale site in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $W$ be such a scheme, let $N\in D(\widehat R_W)$, and let $q:Q\to N$ be any flat-term K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W} B_{W,n}$, $r_n(z)=z\otimes1$ and $\tau_n=1\otimes(B_{W,n+1}\to B_{W,n})$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the strict quotient-semilinear system category on the ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], let $TQ=(Q_n,\tau_n)$, and let $D=U_W(TQ)$ be its restriction to strict towers of $\widehat R_W$-modules. Write $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$, for the canonical simultaneous derived reduction/limit adjunction, with actual unit $u_N$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For a strict tower complex $Z$ put $H(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Z)[-1]$, $s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1})$, with coordinates and differential
$$H(Z)^i=(\prod_n Z_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_n Z_n^i),\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da).$$
Use the normalized Roos identification $\rho_D:H(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WN$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

The strict augmentation $v_Q:Q\to H(D)$, $v_Q(z)=(0,(r_nz)_n)$, is a chain map and satisfies
$$u_N=\rho_D[v_Q][q]^{-1}.$$
This equality is of entire derived morphisms, with zero shifted-product coordinate. More precisely, for any K-injective resolutions with injective terms $a:TQ\to I$ on the ringed sequence site and $j:U_WI\to J$ on its constant-ring tower site [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the composite
$$Q\longrightarrow\lim U_WI\xrightarrow{\lim j}\lim J,\qquad z\longmapsto(a_nr_nz)_n\longmapsto(j_na_nr_nz)_n$$
represents the actual unit after $[q]^{-1}$. The first arrow is the ordinary-adjunction transpose of $a$ for $T\dashv\lim U_W$, and the second is the normalized right-derived composition comparison for restriction of rings followed by sequence projection. Under the canonical inclusion $\lim J\to H(J)$ with zero shifted coordinate, this composite equals $H(jU_W(a))v_Q$. The unit formula is independent of all these resolutions and natural for morphisms of $N$ in the derived category. No completeness or boundedness assumption on $N$ is made.

proof.text: Put $A=\widehat R_W$ and $\mathcal C=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The fixed small skeleton makes both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathbf N_{\geq1}\times\mathcal C$ small in the module universe. The ringed sequence site realizes $\mathscr S_W$, and restriction $U_W$ is exact. By the pro-etale product theorem, countable products in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ are exact; thus the strict Roos comparison in the statement applies to all unbounded tower complexes here. Choose the resolutions $a:TQ\to I$ and $j:U_WI\to J$ with injective terms using K-injective existence on these two small ringed sites. There is no requirement that $U_WI$ itself be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, choice of resolutions; exact-product hypothesis supplied by det-pe-products-exact

proof.text: Let $p$ be the ringed sequence projection with coefficient maps $A\to B_{W,n}$. Its ordinary inverse-image functor on modules is $T(M)=(M\otimes_A B_{W,n})_n$, and $p_*M=\lim U_WM$. Explicitly, the adjunction sends $h:M\to\lim U_WZ$ to the family $m\otimes b\mapsto b\pi_nh(m)$; the inverse sends $f:TM\to Z$ to $m\mapsto(f_n(m\otimes1))_n$. These formulas respect balancing, restrictions and transitions and are inverse, so they also give the termwise complex adjunction. In particular the transpose of $a:TQ\to I$ is the chain map $b:Q\to\lim U_WI$ with $\pi_nb=a_nr_n$. Indeed $t^I_na_{n+1}r_{n+1}=a_n\tau_nr_{n+1}=a_nr_n$; and $d(a_nr_n)=a_nr_nd$ since both factors are chain maps.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; ordinary sequence-projection correspondence of lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction

proof.text: Use the canonical derived adjunction $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$. The sequence-projection theorem identifies $Lp^*N$ with the strict quotient complex $TQ$, and states that its Hom correspondence extends the ordinary one on derived fractions. The resolving-adjunction normalization therefore computes the transpose of the identity of $Lp^*N$ as follows: represent that identity by the resolution map $a:TQ\to I$ and apply the ordinary transpose of Step 2. Consequently the unit $N\to Rp_*Lp^*N$, under the resolution identification $Rp_*[TQ]\simeq[\lim U_WI]$, is $[b][q]^{-1}$. Here the flat-term K-flat hypothesis on $Q$ supplies the left derived representative; K-injectivity of $I$ supplies the right derived representative. This argument computes the unit itself, rather than characterizing it by its level projections.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, with the recorded resolving-adjunction normalization

proof.text: Factor $p$ as the change of rings $c:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathbf N\times\mathcal C),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathbf N\times\mathcal C),\Delta A)$ followed by the constant-ring sequence projection $\pi$. Applied to the constant sequence $A$, the sequence-site equivalence identifies $\Delta A$-module sheaves on $\mathbf N\times\mathcal C$ with $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ componentwise; hence K-injective complexes with injective terms on either side correspond, and the K-injective $J$ below is a K-injective tower with injective terms. Then $c_*=U_W$ and $\pi_*=\lim$, while exactness of $U_W$ identifies $Rc_*$ with $U_W$ on the derived category. Apply the normalized right-derived direct-image composition theorem to the K-injective $I$ and the resolution $j:c_*I\to J$. It says that $\lim j:\lim U_WI\to\lim J$ is a quasi-isomorphism representing the canonical comparison $Rp_*\simeq R\lim U_W$. The sequence pushforward/limit theorem transports the adjunction along this comparison, giving exactly the simultaneous reduction/limit adjunction of the statement. Thus, in the model $\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WN\simeq[\lim J]$, its actual unit is $[b'][q]^{-1}$, where $b'=(\lim j)b$ has coordinates $j_na_nr_n$. This proves the two-resolution assertion with its specified composition normalization.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied to ring restriction and sequence projection; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint

proof.text: Set $\gamma(z)=(r_nz)_n$. The quotient maps give $\tau_nr_{n+1}=r_n$, hence $(1-s_D)\gamma=0$, and $d\gamma=\gamma d$. Therefore the displayed differential gives $d v_Q(z)=d(0,\gamma z)=(0,\gamma dz)=v_Q(dz)$, proving that $v_Q$ is a chain map. Put $f=jU_W(a):D\to J$. It is a strict tower chain map, so $f_nt^D_n=t^J_nf_{n+1}$ implies $(\prod f_n)(1-s_D)=(1-s_J)(\prod f_n)$. Accordingly $H(f)$ acts by $\prod f_n$ on each coordinate. If $\iota_J:\lim J\to H(J)$ is the canonical inclusion, both chain maps $H(f)v_Q$ and $\iota_Jb'$ send $z$ to $(0,(j_na_nr_nz)_n)$; they are equal, including the shifted-product coordinate.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; explicit calculation with the cone differential fixed in the item

proof.text: Since $U_W$ is exact, $f=jU_W(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and is, through the sequence-site equivalence for $\Delta A$ of Step 4, a K-injective tower resolution of $D$ in $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ with injective degree terms. Apply the normalized strict Roos comparison to this resolution: $\iota_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and, under the canonical $R\lim D\simeq[\lim J]$ identification, $\rho_D=[\iota_J]^{-1}[H(f)]$. Step 5 now gives $\rho_D[v_Q]=[\iota_J]^{-1}[H(f)v_Q]=[b']$. Substituting Step 4 yields $u_N=\rho_D[v_Q][q]^{-1}$. The equality is obtained by cancellation of an isomorphism in the derived category, so it is an equality of whole morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, normalized strict Roos resolution comparison

proof.text: The resolutions $a,j$ above were arbitrary of the stated kind, so their formula always represents the same unit. The Roos comparison is resolution-independent and natural, and the simultaneous adjunction has a natural unit. Explicitly, for $h:N\to N'$ its naturality gives $(\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W h)u_N=u_{N'}h$; replacing each unit by the equality of Step 6 gives precisely the naturality of the asserted representative formula. Different choices of $q$, $a$ or $j$ therefore give the same morphism under the canonical derived identifications. All constructions used unbounded K-flat and K-injective representatives and exact countable products; none required completeness or a cohomological bound on $N$.
